chapter: Last job, serenades and New Orleans venues
title: Serenades and muting with derby, tomato can and hand
summary: He serenaded neighbours softly, using a derby, tomato can or hand wah-wah to mute the horn.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: And when he used to come and serenade us at 2 o'clock in the morning, where we live now, visit the sacred heart conference. Well, the nuns used to tell the children, the boys, you know, and they were living right in the back of them, who was playing the music last night? He said, we certainly did enjoy that music. It was fine. It was fine. Nobody in the neighborhood complained about him playing. They used to play so low with those music. Yes. You know, it was pretty. It was really pretty. With the old, I mean, when we had that old horn, they wasn't using mute like they're doing now, you know.
No, not open, the open horn, yes. And he used to, he had an old derby, and he gelt that derby. I said, but you didn't gelt that derby for. And he put it over the bell. Yeah, he put it over there.
Do you remember what kind of pieces they would play out on the, those serenades when they would serenade people?

I can't remember the name of the piece. I think you told me three o'clock in the morning for one. You played three o'clock in the morning, but there was a special waltz they used to play when they go out. But I can't call them. Was it the klema waltz? No, the klema waltz. I can't remember the name.
It was sort of soft, quiet music, like waltz. Very, very soft. Yeah, soft waltz.
And for the old corn egg, he had a tomato can, and he gelt that.
Oh, and use it for a mute.
And just hold it in for, you know, for mute.
Oh, yeah. Oh, and for the bell of the horn.
I've seen people use water glass or even a coconut shell. Anything to muffle a tone.
And then when you get that wah-wah. Oh, he could do that. You know how to mute, you know, the wah-wah.
He just put his hand over it. Yeah, just use the hand, and somebody should use a toilet flush. Yeah, so it's rubber plungers sometimes. Yeah, plungers.
It used to sound like it was crying, you know, kind of like a baby crying.
He doesn't know how to sound like that. Yes, he could really do that.
